correctness.rationale: For the complete projective direction set P1(Z/N), weighted line-sum normalization sqrt(w_d/N) gives T_w*T_w diagonal in normalized Fourier characters with eigenvalue lambda_xi=sum_{<xi,d>=0}w_d. For primitive nonzero xi, there is exactly one perpendicular projective direction, and every direction is realized; hence the nonconstant minimal eigenvalue is min w_d. For any nonzero xi, choose a prime p with nonzero p-primary component; its reduction constrains all orthogonal directions to one mod-p projective fiber, yielding lambda_xi<=W_{p,ell}; conversely a character whose p^k local coordinate is p^(k-1) times a perpendicular nonzero mod-p vector and other local components vanish realizes *exactly* W_{p,ell}. Thus maximum is max_{p|N,ell} W_{p,ell}. Average over least-prime p_* fibers and min w_d <=S/D_N gives sharp kappa_0²>=D_N/(p_*+1), with equality only if all direction weights coincide. Local CRT count of orthogonality directions (p^v for nonzero local valuation v, p^(k-1)(p+1) for zero) and local frequency multiplicities p^{2(k-v)}-p^{2(k-v-1)} exhaust N² characters, proving full uniform spectrum. Independent construction of projective sets and weighted nonzero character eigenvalues for N=2..14 confirmed min/max and D_N, not infinity.
risks: Finite tests N<=14 do not establish arbitrary composite N; the proof uses local CRT and exact valuation combinatorics.
Condition number is restricted to the mean-zero subspace and uniform scalar per direction; arbitrary line or frequency filtering is a different problem.

value.rationale: Cyclic projective Radon transforms and scalar acquisition weights are natural discrete tomography objects. The theorem quantifies a sharp arithmetic conditioning barrier tied to the smallest prime, identifies the uniquely best positive view schedule and supplies exact mode multiplicities. It is mathematically useful even where more general frequency filtering can do better.
